thread:
maria: Quick sync — we need one consistent signal for 'client-initiated stream teardown' vs 'server abort' across the gateway and edge proxy. RFC follow-up from last week.

devin: +1. current behaviour mixes HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and a trailers-based `x-redwood-terminal` header. messy when proxies sit in front.

maria: Exactly. That causes double-counting retries and incorrect billing attribution when proxies translate signals. We should pick one canonical wire-level primitive.

olga: My vote is: keep transport-agnostic semantic at the gateway layer (an intent header) and let edge map to transport-specific control frames. means: prefer a lightweight header/tag rather than relying on RST or TCP close.

sachin: agree on semantic layer, but what about midflight partial responses? client might cancel after receiving partial tokens; server still wants to finish background cleanup. We need to encode reason + idempotency-safety.

devin: proposal: `X-Redwood-Terminate: reason=<client|server|timeout>; id=<opaque>` as a trailer for HTTP/1.1 and a metadata frame for h2/quic. gateway treats it as authoritative for billing/telemetry.

maria: that covers reason and ties events, good. how do proxies that don't understand the header behave? we need backwards compatibility.

olga: fallback: proxies that don't parse it will keep current behavior, but the gateway will emit a short-lived control event to the edge control plane with the same id so observability/chargeback is consistent. outline: if header present, gateway records termination event and suppresses automatic retry-path hedging.

sachin: sample mapping for h2/quic: map `X-Redwood-Terminate` -> `GRPC:terminal` frame (proposed) and on RST_STREAM we annotate with `reason=transport`. include code snippet for parsing: 

```
// pseudocode
if (trailers.contains("X-Redwood-Terminate")) {
  let t = parse(trailers["X-Redwood-Terminate"])
  metrics.emitTermination(id=t.id, reason=t.reason, source="client")
  disableUpstreamRetry(request.id)
}
```

devin: one more: we need id collision protection. make id = sha256(req-id || timestamp || node-id) and limit lifetime to 30s.

maria: sounds reasonable. operational concerns: does this increase control-plane chatter? if gateway emits events, could be lots during bursty streams.

olga: keep control events minimal: only emit when trailer present or when server signals graceful-terminate. non-terminal RSTs don't auto-emit. also sample at 1% for heavy tenants.

sachin: what about retry semantics downstream? if gateway sees client-terminate, it must not trigger automatic hedges or replay on fallback model. that avoids duplicate side-effects.

devin: agreed. add a short-circuit: if termination.reason == client -> treat as non-idempotent unless request metadata contains `idempotent=true`.

maria: operational checklist for implementation: (1) add trailer/header parsing at gateway ingest, (2) canonicalize id generation, (3) emit termination event to control plane with TTL, (4) teach hedging layer to consult termination cache, (5) document rule for backends.

olga: I'll draft a brief RFC patch with mapping table for HTTP/1.1, h2, quic and a compatibility paragraph. ping me for review. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new feature branch created: `feature/terminate-header-support` — CI pipeline queued.

maria: thanks — let's aim for a small canary behind a flag. please add unit tests for collision TTL and hedging short-circuit.

devin: adding test notes to the RFC. also will add a debug flag to surface termination decisions in traces.

sachin: also add a CLI tool to inspect active termination cache entries for oncall. saves time during incidents.

maria: perfect. if no objections I'll merge the patch to the RFC draft tomorrow.

olga: no objections from me.

devin: lgtm.

sachin: lgtm.

maria: closing this thread for now — will post RFC link when ready. :wave:
